title: The join family
summary: Which join keeps the rows that matched nothing, what the padding does to the next clause you write, and the two spellings of "has none".

cards.front: `INNER JOIN` and `LEFT JOIN`, same `ON` condition. What is in one result and not the other?
cards.back: The left rows that matched nothing, which `LEFT` keeps with NULL in every right-hand column. A self-join of 12 `employees` on `manager_id` gives 11 rows inner and 12 left, because the CEO has no manager.

cards.front: Two orders, one with two line items and one with three. How many rows does `orders JOIN order_items` return?
cards.back: Five: a join produces pairs, so a left row repeats once per matching right row. A duplicated name, an inflated `SUM` and a `COUNT` that is too big are this one bug.

cards.front: The customers with no completed orders vanished from the report, and the `LEFT JOIN` is still in the source. What happened?
cards.back: A condition on the right-hand table went into `WHERE` instead of `ON`. The padded rows hold NULL there, the comparison is not true, and `WHERE` drops them: 8 customers instead of 10.

cards.front: Which test on a right-hand column survives a `LEFT JOIN`, and what does it get you?
cards.back: `IS NULL`, which gets you the anti-join: the left rows that matched nothing. Test the primary key, since `WHERE r.comment IS NULL` also catches the 10 real reviews with no comment.

cards.front: What does `FULL OUTER JOIN` add that `LEFT JOIN` does not?
cards.back: The unmatched rows from the right-hand table too, so an order whose customer row is missing comes back with NULL in every customer column.

cards.front: What is a `CROSS JOIN`, and what does every other join have to do with it?
cards.back: The cartesian product: 10 customers and 20 orders give 200 rows. Every join starts there, and `ON` is a filter keeping only the pairs it evaluates true for.

cards.front: `WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT manager_id FROM employees)` came back empty, with no error. Why?
cards.back: One `manager_id` is NULL, and a comparison against NULL is unknown, so `NOT IN` can never be true for anybody. The same question as `NOT EXISTS` returns all 9 employees who manage nobody.

cards.front: `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE r.id IS NULL` and `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 ...)` return the same rows. Which do you reach for?
cards.back: `NOT EXISTS`, whenever the right-hand table contributes no columns to the output, which is most of the time. It builds no pairs and stops at the first match.
